//: Type-checks client/test/*.test.ts AND client/js/**/*.js under the same compiler run.
client/js/*.js stays plain JS on disk — it is served straight to the browser via a bare
<script type="module"> with no bundler in front of it (see client/index.html), and none of
these files are renamed to .ts/.tsx, so the runtime is byte-identical to what shipped before.
checkJs makes tsc read the JSDoc annotations already in each .js file (or infer types from
usage where JSDoc is absent) and enforce them exactly as it would for real .ts — this is the
mechanism, not a build step. The remaining sidecar .d.ts files in client/js/ declare test-only
shapes (e.g. a headless DOM stand-in) that have no corresponding real export and so cannot be
expressed as JSDoc on the .js they accompany; where a .d.ts merely restated a .js's own
exports it was deleted in favor of the .js's own JSDoc as the single source of truth.
